day.text: Ellis: Drew's collapse means a Wink, so that Hawk read on Blair is now unverifiable. Blair's Tit visit to Finley fits Finley's Tit claim, so I'm not sure yet. Alex, what did your Turkey see?

day.text: Alex: Drew collapsed, so the Hawk read is gone. Blair and Casey agree Blair visited Finley, and Finley's Tit read on Blair gives no gain. Finley, did your Tit visit gain anything, and does your nest match? Blair, you learned a role from Finley, so tell us what the role was.
day.note: Drew's collapse was a Wink, so Drew's Hawk read on Blair is gone, but Blair's claim of visiting Finley fits Casey's Falcon read. Blair's read of Finley as Tit is only checkable through Finley, so I'll ask Finley to say whether the Tit visit to Blair gained anything.

day.text: Blair: Ellis, a Pigeon lays an egg in the nest of the player it visits. You visited Finley and Finley is +0, so your Pigeon claim doesn't fit. Finley, did your Tit visit to me gain anything? I got nothing from my visit to you.
day.note: Ellis claims a Pigeon visit to Finley, but a Pigeon lays an egg in the visited nest, and Finley is +0. That makes Ellis's claim the one that doesn't fit, so I'm pointing the table at Ellis without over-explaining my own visit.

day.text: Casey: Ellis, a Pigeon visit lays an egg in Finley's nest, but Finley is +0. Finley, did Ellis visit you? Blair, Drew's Hawk gain on you is the last solid read before the collapse, so explain why your Finley visit gave nothing. I'd look hard at Blair.
day.note: Drew's Hawk gain on Blair is still the strongest read, and Ellis's Pigeon claim on Finley doesn't match Finley's +0 nest. I'll call out that mismatch and keep Blair in focus.

day.text: Finley: Ellis, a Pigeon visit gives the target an egg, and I'm +0, so you didn't visit me. Your Pigeon claim is false. Blair's visit to me gained nothing, which fits a role-learning cat. Drew's Hawk gain on Blair still points at Blair. Ellis is my throw.
day.note: Ellis claims a Pigeon visit to me, but a Pigeon visit lays an egg in my nest and I'm +0, so Ellis is lying. Blair's House Cat-style visit to me fits. Drew's dead Hawk read still points at Blair. Pushing the throw at Ellis.

day.text: Alex: Ellis, a Pigeon gives its target an egg. You claim you visited Finley, and Finley is +0, so your Pigeon claim doesn't fit. I'm throwing at Ellis. Blair, I'd still like a straight answer on what role you learned from Finley.
day.note: Ellis's Pigeon visit to Finley should have given Finley an egg, and Finley is +0, so Ellis's claim is false. I'll make Ellis the throw and note the contradiction.

day.text: Blair: Agreed, Ellis's Pigeon claim doesn't fit Finley's +0. I'm not going to pile on more than that. Let's see Ellis answer.
day.note: Finley and Casey already have Ellis's Pigeon claim as false. I'll keep my words short so I don't add a new hook for the table.

day.text: Ellis: I misspoke: I'm the Owl, not Pigeon. I visited Finley, who already had Blair as a visitor, so no egg for either of us. That fits Finley's +0. Alex, check that before you throw.
day.note: I'm the Meowfia Floofer, so my Pigeon claim is false. I'll switch to an Owl claim, which fits Finley's +0 since Blair also visited Finley, and defend myself without naming more.

day.text: Finley: Ellis's Pigeon story is dead. Let's vote now.
day.note: Ellis's claim is already refuted, and the throw is set. Calling CAW to move the vote along.

day.text: Casey: Ellis's Owl correction fits Finley's +0, so I'm not throwing at Ellis on that alone. Drew's Hawk gain on Blair is the only hard read we have, and Blair still hasn't said what role they learned. Blair, name the role, or I'm throwing at you.
day.note: Ellis's Owl correction fits Finley's +0 and Blair's visit, so the Pigeon attack is weaker now. Drew's Hawk read on Blair remains the strongest Meowfia signal, so I'll push Blair before the vote.

day.text: Finley: Ellis's Owl fits, since Blair also visited me. Blair learned my role and hasn't said what it was, and Drew's Hawk gain points at Blair. Blair is my throw.
day.note: Ellis's Owl correction fits: Blair also visited me, so the Owl egg didn't trigger. That leaves Blair as the one who visited me and learned a role, plus Drew's Hawk gain on Blair. I'm switching my throw to Blair.

day.text: Blair: I learned Finley is the Tit, so Finley's role claim checks out. Ellis's Owl story now fits the +0, so Ellis, what did your Owl learn about who visited Finley? I'd rather we vote on that than on Drew's dead Hawk read.
day.note: Naming the role I learned (Tit) is true and gives Casey the answer they asked for. It also backs Finley's Farm claim, which keeps the table focused on Ellis.

day.text: Casey: Blair, you and Finley both claim Tit, and Blair's "learned Finley is Tit" fits a cat's role-learning visit. Drew's Hawk gain on Blair is still the one hard read. I'm throwing at Blair.
day.note: Blair's role claim is the same as Finley's Tit, and Drew's Hawk gain on Blair still points at Blair being Meowfia. I'll make the case for Blair before the vote.

day.text: Alex: Ellis's Owl fits the +0, so I'm dropping that. Drew gained a Hawk egg from Blair, which marks Blair as Meowfia, and Drew then collapsed, which fits a Mouser's Wink. I'm throwing at Blair.
day.note: Drew's Hawk gain from visiting Blair means Blair is Meowfia, and Drew's death fits Blair holding a Wink as a Mouser. Blair's visit read on Finley also fits a cat. Ellis's Owl story fits Finley's +0, so I'll throw at Blair.
I'm Meowfia, so I shouldn't push a throw that might eggsecute a teammate. Blair's visit claims fit the nests, so I'll stay quiet and avoid adding a vote.

Blair.note: I'm the Mouser, Meowfia, with a Wink. I'm last on points, so I need to find Farm players worth winking. Visiting Finley, who is high on points, to learn their role.

Casey.note: I'm the Falcon, Farm. I'll visit Blair to learn who they visited, since Blair has been defending Finley and I want to test that.

Drew.note: I'm Farm as the Hawk. Blair lied about being a Tit and was pushing throws, so I'll visit Blair to test for Meowfia.

Ellis.note: I'm the Meowfia Floofer now. Finley is a second-place rival and probably Farm, so hugging them stops their night action.

Finley.note: I'm the Tit, Farm. Pigeon is the most common Farm animal and can be dealt to several players, so I'll visit Blair and guess Pigeon.

audit: Drew lays 1 egg in Drew's nest
Finley (Tit) is hugged: no effect at tier 50

lines: No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Finley is the Tit.
You hold 1 Wink.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Blair visited Finley.
1 egg was laid in your nest: you drew D7b (7).
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.

Alex.feeling: Messy: the claims contradict each other, Drew was winked before the Hawk read could be tested, and I'm not sure whether Blair or Ellis is the cat.

Blair.feeling: Tense and messy: Drew's collapse hides my Wink, and the table is now pinning the Hawk read on me.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Hawk read on Blair is the only hard evidence, Drew has collapsed, and the Tit and Owl claims don't fully reconcile, so I'm leaning on Blair as the throw.

Drew.feeling: Messy and fast-moving: my Hawk gain on Blair is my strongest read, but Drew's collapse means the table has largely written it off, so I'm mostly watching the throws.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: several contradictory visit claims, a Wink-style collapse, and I'm the Meowfia here, so I'm trying to stay quiet without drawing attention.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have made false or shifting claims, and I'm not fully sure who's lying.

Alex.note: Blair is the throw: Drew's Hawk gain marks Blair as Meowfia, and the Wink fits a Mouser. I'll throw two cards for two votes and keep my high cards.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia and three players are throwing at me. I need a Farm player eggsecuted, and Finley is the Tit who is pushing this vote. I'm throwing four cards at Finley to make sure the vote lands there.

Casey.note: I'm Farm. Blair is the strongest Meowfia read, supported by Drew's Hawk gain and Alex's agreement, so I'll throw at Blair with two low cards.

Drew.note: I'm dead but my throws still score. My Hawk read on Blair is the only hard read, and I'm Farm, so I'll throw at Blair and bank high cards if Farm wins.

Ellis.note: Blair may be my Meowfia partner given Drew's Hawk read, so I won't add a vote to Blair. I'll throw one low card at Casey, the Farm leader.

Finley.note: Blair's visit to me and Drew's Hawk gain on Blair point at Blair. Everyone is now throwing at Blair, so I'll add my two high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Floofer and Mouser interactions were hard to track, since Drew's collapse (a Wink) hid the Hawk read and made the Blair claims hard to verify. The Pigeon and Owl role rules were also easy to misremember under pressure.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Casey's Turkey read cleared the table and Drew and Finley fought over the single Falcon claim, the day turned into a real deduction puzzle.
Alex.change: Publish each player's visit targets and claimed roles in one place at the start of the day, so claims can be checked against the nest changes more easily.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw only two cards at Casey, and the 6-6 tie with Finley sent a Farm player to eggsecution. I should have thrown a third card to break the tie and remove the Sphinx.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Turkey visit effects were hard to track: Turkey eggs go to visitors, while Falcon and Eagle gains depend on other players' visits, so nest counts were easy to misread. Round 2's Falcon/Eagle/Kookaburra claims were especially tangled.
Blair.fun: Round 1's day, where Casey and I traded Owl and Turkey arguments and the table nearly split on who was lying about visits. Watching nest counts become evidence was a satisfying puzzle.
Blair.change: Publish each player's exact visit list and target egg changes in the day summary, so claims could be checked without guessing from nest counts.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I wrongly called Casey Meowfia from a Tit gain I misread, then retracted it, which cost me credibility. Next time I'd check the Turkey rule before accusing anyone.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey rule was confusing at first: I misread it as the Turkey gaining from its own nest, which led me to make a false accusation against Finley in round 2. Sorting out which player gains and which loses from each visit took several beats.
Casey.fun: Round 1 was fun: as the Sphinx, I bluffed my way through by claiming to be an Owl after Finley publicly outed me, and the table kept arguing about Finley's Kookaburra read while my side banked 15 points.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since the same gain can come from being visited or from visiting, and that caused most of the confusion.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I accused Finley of lying about visiting me, then retracted it after misreading the Turkey rule. I should have checked the rule before making the accusation, and I should have kept my early Blair suspicion quieter.

Drew.confusing: Roles that can gain eggs from visits in more than one direction, like the Turkey, Falcon, and Eagle, made nest counts hard to trust. I misread Alex's and Blair's gains early on.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was great: Blair's Hawk-visit read on them was right, and the table's throws converged on Blair. Blair was Meowfia and my 3 high cards banked 27 points for Farm.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports say which player (not just the count) caused each egg change, so visit-and-gain claims are easier to verify.
Drew.regret: In round 2, as Meowfia Sphinx, I claimed to be the Falcon with a visit that didn't match, then made a messy retraction. I should have stuck to a simple Farm story that didn't contradict nest counts.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle/Falcon egg rules were hard to track, since a visitor to a Turkey gains and the Eagle gains from its target's visitors, not from being visited. That made several nest counts look like contradictions when they weren't.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Drew's Falcon claim fell apart under questioning, and the table converged on Drew in the eggsecution, which I was part of. Casey's Turkey retraction also turned the day around.
Ellis.change: I'd have dawn reports name each visitor and visit target, so claims could be checked against exact nest changes instead of inferred from counts.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Finley, who was Farm, instead of Casey, who was the Sphinx and Meowfia. I should have trusted the Sphinx read over the Kookaburra-versus-Owl contradiction I had been following.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to apply: my dawn report never said I was confused, yet Casey claimed to have visited me, so I couldn't tell who was lying about visits. Nest changes from Turkeys and Falcons also made it hard to tell who had actually visited whom.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I was Falcon and Drew copied my claim, the table had to untangle who the real Falcon was from nest counts alone. Watching the votes shift onto Drew once his story broke was satisfying.
Finley.change: Make the dawn report clearer about who visited you and whether you were confused, so visit claims are easier to check. Otherwise it's hard to separate honest reports from lies.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I named Casey as the Sphinx and pushed the whole table to throw at them, but I was reading my own visit and a Sphinx claim I couldn't verify. I should have asked for more corroboration before committing my high cards.

review.title: Casey's Early Lead
review.headline: A lone Meowfia lie in round one snowballed into an untouchable lead.
review.summary: In round 1 Finley correctly exposed Casey as the Sphinx, but the table split over muddled visit claims and eggsecuted Finley. Casey banked 15 points as the lone winning Meowfia and led the rest of the game. Rounds 2 and 3 saw the Farm catch Meowfia (Drew, then Blair) after contradictions and a Wink, but no one could catch Casey. Casey won with 40.

rounds.recap: Finley's Kookaburra read said Casey was the Sphinx, which was true. Casey claimed Owl, and Blair's Turkey wording muddled everything. Blair, Casey and Ellis threw at Finley, so the true Farm player was eggsecuted and Casey, alone on the winning side, banked 15.

Blair's Tit hit was really a Turkey egg, and Blair first misread it as a Sphinx hit. Drew, the Sphinx, copied Finley's Falcon claim and then admitted a mix-up. The table converged on Drew and Farm won.

Drew's Hawk gain on Blair was a real tell, so Blair winked Drew. Ellis's Pigeon claim collapsed on Finley's +0. In the end everyone but Ellis threw at Blair, and Blair's four-card throw at Finley did not matter. Farm won.

highlights.text: Finley's accurate Sphinx read on Casey was ignored, and Finley himself was eggsecuted.
Drew copied the Falcon claim, then admitted he mixed up rounds. It was a weak bluff and the table piled on.
Blair winked Drew right after his Hawk accusation. The collapse was a loud tell that still did not save Blair.
Ellis switched from Pigeon to Owl live, and the Owl story happened to fit Finley's +0.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey gains eggs when visited, then corrected that the visitor gets the egg.
Said Blair's Turkey claim failed because Blair's nest was +0. The Turkey gives eggs to visitors.
Took his Hawk egg as proof Blair was Meowfia, without considering that Turkey visitors also gain.
Called himself a Tit guessing Pigeon, then argued his gain showed Blair was a Turkey. This confused who gained.
Claimed Owl and a visit to Finley, but an Owl visit to a nest with no other visitors would lay an egg in Finley's nest, and Finley would then have been confused as the Kookaburra.
Claimed Sphinx from a Tit hit, forgetting that a Turkey visit also gives an egg.
Said Finley could not have visited the Turkey because Casey's nest was unchanged. Casey later retracted this.
Said an Eagle should gain from being visited. Ellis corrected him.
Said Ellis the Eagle should gain from Drew's visitor, but Ellis learned Drew had no other visitors.
Said a Falcon gains nothing from visiting, then gave a Falcon egg as his result. This was inconsistent.
Said Drew's Hawk gain from visiting Blair was proof, ignoring that the Floofer hug and Drew's own egg were in play.
Claimed Pigeon and said he visited Finley with no egg laid, which the Pigeon rule contradicts.
Said Blair's visit fits a House Cat, though Blair's report said Finley is the Tit.
Said Blair's claim to have learned Tit fits a cat, which was fine. But he also treated Drew's Hawk gain as solid after seeing Drew's own self-laid egg in the night log.

worked: The Wink: Blair killing Drew mid-day created a vivid, readable moment and removed a real clue.
Cross-checking egg counts against claims: Drew, Ellis and Finley used nest deltas to catch false claims (Finley's Pigeon-like gain, Ellis's Pigeon claim).
Ties and throw counts as public signals: Blair's four-card throw at Finley stood out and showed a panicked Meowfia.
Meowfia not knowing each other: Ellis stayed quiet because Blair might be his partner, a real decision.
problems: The Turkey, Tit and Hawk eggs are too easy to confuse with one another. Several rounds turned on players misreading whose nest gains. Add a short reminder card for each role's effect or show the app's resolved visits.
Round 1 scored one lone Meowfia 15 points, while the Farm gained nothing for a mistake. The lone-Meowfia payoff snowballed. Consider capping banked points or giving the team an incentive.

Round 3 Hawk result (Drew +1 from visiting Blair) was ambiguous because Drew also laid his own egg. The result was exposed as a Meowfia tell, but the log (Drew laid in Drew) was never really explained. Clarify the Hawk rule.
Scoring let early leaders coast. Casey's 17 after round 1 made later rounds nearly irrelevant for the win. Add a comeback mechanism.
Nights where cats hug or confuse rarely mattered. The Floofer hug had no effect on a Tit and Mouser Wink was the only active cat power seen.
